meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas. doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.title: Increased mammalian lifespan and a segmental and tissue-specific slowing of aging after genetic reduction of mTOR expression
data.authors: Wu JJ; Finkel T et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Genetically reduced mTOR increases mouse lifespan with tissue-specific slowing of aging.
data.abstract_excerpt: We analyzed aging parameters using a mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) hypomorphic mouse model. Mice with two hypomorphic alleles are viable but express mTOR at approximately 25% of wild-type levels. These animals demonstrate reduced mTORC1 and mTORC2 activity and exhibit an approximately 20% increase in median survival. While these mice are smaller than wild-type mice, they do not demonstrate any alterations in normalized food intake, glucose homeostasis, or metabolic rate. Consistent with their increased lifespan, the mice exhibited a reduction in a number of aging tissue biomarkers.

extracted_findings.effect: Genetic reduction of mTOR extends median lifespan ~20% with segmental, tissue-specific slowing of aging
extracted_findings.dose: mTOR protein reduced to approximately 25% of wild type levels
extracted_findings.sample_size: males: n=17 (mTOR Δ/Δ), n=10 (WT); females: n=26 (mTOR Δ/Δ), n=24 (WT); combined: n=43 (mTOR Δ/Δ), n=34 (WT)
extracted_findings.effect_size: Median survival increased by 22% for males (p=0.02) and 19% for females (p=0.047); overall median survival 30.3 months for mTOR Δ/Δ vs 26.2 months for WT (p=0.0057)
extracted_findings.limitations: Higher euthanasia rate for mTOR Δ/Δ mice due to severe infections (37% vs 17% WT, p<0.01); exacerbated age-dependent decrease in trabecular bone volume and increased age-dependent infections (mouth, eye, skin) in mTOR Δ/Δ mice
